about:
ARCH Hawaii operates from a fabrication studio at 2014 Republican Street in Honolulu, Hawaii. The company describes itself as a local team of designers, builders, artists, and problem-solvers rooted in Hawai'i, though no founding year or individual founders are disclosed in the available materials. Ownership structure is not specified.

The shop runs 3-axis CNC and CNC foam machining equipment to produce scenic fabrication, set construction, prop fabrication, custom millwork, kinetic sculpture, and public art installations. Work spans materials including wood (notably koa), metal (stainless steel 316 mirror polish), foam, and integrated LED lighting. The facility handles projects from tabletop scale up to two-story installations, offering concept development, production design, CAD, and 3D renderings through its creative studio, plus delivery, rigging, site coordination, and strike services.

Clients come from film and television production (Netflix, NCIS), commercial advertising (LEGO, Nike, Louis Vuitton, The Macallan), retail design (Bank of Hawaii, Meta Lab, Le Monde, Soho House), public art and museums (Hawaii Contemporary, Mission Houses Museum), live entertainment (Cirque du Soleil 'Auana), and corporate branding (Amazon, NBC, MTV, Pandora, The North Face). Broadcast work runs on IATSE union crews built to camera tolerance on fixed schedules.

The company positions its differentiator as combining local Hawaiian craftsmanship with creative thinking and hands-on problem solving to "build what others only imagine," emphasizing a concept-through-installation workflow under one roof, union-qualified crews for broadcast, and island-sourced, eco-conscious materials.
